title: Retrofit and OkHttp: calls, errors, retries and interceptors

videos.script: Until now the planner's sessions lived on the phone. This lesson connects it to a server, and spends most of its time on what goes wrong. {{api}} First, the contract: three requests, written as a Kotlin interface. Retrofit writes the rest. {{server}} Then a real server that lives inside the test, and answers whatever the test tells it to. {{errors}} Then the two kinds of failure. The server said no, or nothing came back. They deserve different words on screen. {{retry}} Then time limits, and retries. A request for data may be sent again. A request that saves something may not. {{interceptors}} Then one place for what every request needs: the token, the retry, and a log that never shows the token. {{manifest}} And last, the permission the phone asks about, which a library had already asked for.
